_purpose: Maxi's scene roster: every walk-through rung, 2D first then 3D; `tiles` lists the nine GYM tiles in front-page order. Generated by scripts/gen-memories-roster.mjs from the pinned vendored SDK registry; regenerate to see drift. Every id here has <id>-build*.md, <id>-card.md and <id>-seen.md beside this file.

scenes.prose: A collimated line of quanta drifts steadily along +X, each carrying a small always-armed transverse ripple (λ=16) — the walk in its simplest form.
The same straight walk, but the transverse coin is given leverage — the ripple grows into a visible snake as each leaf oscillates with a longer wavelength.
Release the walk in every direction at once — a single point source spraying an even disk of quanta (the sun). Mixed-axis momentum un-degenerates the direction sampler.
A single omni source of oppositely-charged quanta launched from a ring — the overlapping charged walks braid into radial bands of light and dark, an interference pattern with no wave equation.

A laser, assembled from parts you have already met. A GAIN SOURCE — rung 3's omni emitter, restricted to a forward half-fan — fires into a RESONANT BORE whose walls re-aim every hit forward instead of reflecting it, and the beam leaves through an OUTPUT COUPLER at the far mouth. The coupler has two independent switches: RECENTER collapses every exiting quantum onto the bore's mid-line, making the mouth a single point source; PHASE RESET re-locks the ensemble's oscillation so equal-radius quanta share a phase again. Recentering alone gives you the geometry of rung 4; adding phase gives you its coherence. Sweep the two switches against the wavelength and the bore length: at long wavelengths the mouth is already nearly in phase and the bands appear on their own, while at short ones the fan reads smooth until you switch phase on. Nothing here is a wave equation — it is the same charged walk, aimed and re-timed.
The SAME self-interference field, worn as water — particles hidden and the water shader on. The light field and the water field are the same emergent wave, a different lens (the fractal aha).

tile.title: A pool
tile.tile: One source. Rings. Interference as the geometry of random walks, not a wave.
tile.what: One source, and rings of ripples spread out across the water, glinting like light on a pool.
tile.why: A ray is a straight line with no wave in it, so ray tracing cannot make interference rings at any cost, and solving the waves directly runs into the costs in the intro.
tile.how: One sphere emitter - classical mechanics that looks like water, from the same light object, the sphere emitter that made the sun in the previous scene. Every particle zig-zags as it travels, so its path is itself a wave; the rings are the geometry of those wavy random walks crossing. The water is the same light field shown through a different renderer. No equations.

still.alt: A dark teal surface scattered with white glints like light on water, with a faint ring around a dark dot at its centre.

scenes.prose: Two independent self-interference sources, ±32px apart — their overlapping charged walks form an interference lattice between them: pure density superposition of two IID populations, interference without a wave equation.
The two-source lattice worn as water — two fountains whose ripple fields overlap into the same interference web, painted by the water shader with the particles hidden.
The two-source field lit as plasma — particles ON, water surface, and an additive bloom, so the two colliding charged streams read as a fusing plasma core.

The first true routing demo: a LASER — a genuinely collimated +x beam (the tightest emission the emitter supports: pure +x momentum, a single charge, no wavelength-scale spreading) — fires into a rotatable mirror. The mirror compiles the real reflection law: a surface tilted to θ deflects the beam by 2θ (standard optics), so at 45° the thin beam exits straight up. ROTATE the mirror (the orientation slider, or LOOK-x in 3D) and the thin reflected beam steers live.

A wall that ABSORBS the quanta into its OWN real mass — it fills as it soaks up arrivals, stops at capacity, and slowly radiates the stored mass back out as lower-dimension leaves. Mass is exactly conserved (the blackbody absorb/re-emit).

A detector screen — the Detector Screen preset (destroy + count) tallies every arrival by position. A LIVE in-scene chart (a first-class LiveChart object placed beside the detector) plots the running y→count histogram as the sim runs — the chart reads wall.getCollisionHistogram between ticks and accumulates on-screen. This is the basis for the double-slit fringe readout. The chart panel is a plain render-only object: drag it, resize it, or point it at any counting wall.

The explanatory centerpiece: a single 2-PARTICLE-WIDE laser threads a CLOSED TEN-MIRROR {10/3} STAR and LOOPS FOREVER — m1→m2→…→m10→m1→… with no exit. Ten tall/thin mirrors sit at the vertices of a regular decagon; each mirror's tilt is solved from its incoming/outgoing chords so the reflected centre-line hits the next mirror exactly, and by the star's symmetry the tenth leg feeds straight back into the first — the polygon closes on itself. Each mirror is a DIFFERENT colour and, on collision, TAGS the beam with its own colour (its drawn colour = its identity): so a particle's colour history IS its bounce sequence — red after m1, orange after m2, … magenta after m10, then red again as it re-enters the loop (a pkg-node colour-transition proof shows the dominant next-colour after m_k is m_{k+1} for all ten, closing the ring). Reflection off the DRAWN face is the standard-optics 2θ law (the swept-OBB face collision), ten times over, no wave equation. In 3D (the default mode) every mirror is a SLAB — a plate with real depth — standing at its decagon vertex with the same in-plane tilt, and the laser is volumetric: it braids in y AND z, each slab's tilted faces reflect it by the 2θ law (vz passes through) and its near/far z-faces bounce vz, so no mirror passes the beam; ORBIT the camera (LOOK/drag or the az/el sliders) to see the ring as plates in space, and z-strays exit between the slabs and die at the scene's z-boundary. Switch the MODE strip to 2D for the flat star — the same ring, tilts, colours and laser, minus the z-axis (2D≡3D). Because the loop has no sink, the beam never leaves — an INVISIBLE background Wall (nothing + count hook) spanning the whole canvas (and, in 3D, the whole volume) counts the live population every tick (its per-tick collided frames ARE the live quanta), and the emitter's DECLARED emission gate (emissionCap + gateCounter, the blackbody pattern compiled at construction) reads THAT counter to pause emission at the cap and resume below it, so the population plateaus and FPS stays healthy while the circuit runs indefinitely — and the gate survives Restart (it is captured descriptor DATA, not recipe code).

tile.title: Infinite mirror
tile.tile: Ten mirrors in a ring. Light walks the loop. No Fresnel equations.
tile.what: Ten mirrors in a ring. Light goes round and round the loop, reflected and diffused from mirror to mirror, each mirror colouring the light it sends on.
tile.why: Conventional renderers cut every light path off after a set number of bounces and treat shadows, reflections and indirect light as separate effects. Solving the light directly in a 5 m room would take Frontier about 3 billion years.
tile.how: One emitter and ten walls set as mirrors. Light leaves in every direction; shadowing, reflection and obstruction are all live, with no limit on the objects in its path, and the diffusion is real. No Fresnel equations.

still.alt: Ten brightly coloured mirrors in a ring, seen from above; a dense band of gold, orange and green dots circles a dark, empty centre inside it, and faint gold and green rays fan out from that light between the mirrors into the dark space around.

scenes.prose: The double-slit REBUILT ON THE TUNNEL OBJECT at PHYSICAL DSE PROPORTIONS: the detector sits at the SYMMETRIC distance — emitter-to-front of the slit wall EQUALS back of the slit wall-to-detector. Each slit channel is a DIRECTED Tunnel: a hit on a channel wall ejects the quantum back into the bore and re-emits it in a uniformly random direction within 180 degrees of the corridor axis, so each slit acts as a semi-circular emitter — the classical picture of what a slit does to a wavefront — rather than a mirror that would only ever project the beam it was given. The exit angle is drawn with real trig, so the fan is flat, not diagonal-weighted; the barriers + screen are v2 Walls (destroy / detector preset) so the scene survives Restart. The source emits FORWARD over 180 degrees (the hemisphere preset) rather than all the way round, so the burst that used to fly backward into the catcher now lights the aperture — the same sampler, restricted to the forward half, aimed at the wall. In 2D a balanced, central-dominant three-lobe interference pattern builds up. Switch the MODE strip to 3D and the SAME experiment stands up in space — the barrier becomes a plate with two slots, each channel a real corridor, the source a volumetric forward half-ball — and the instrument follows: the detector plate paints its OWN hit map on its faces, exactly where each particle landed, so the fringes read as bands on the plate itself. Identical physics, one more axis (2D≡3D).

tile.title: Double slit
tile.tile: Two slits, one particle at a time. Feynman's “only mystery,” with no amplitudes to add.
tile.what: Particles go through two slits one at a time, and bright and dark bands build up on the detector plate below them, live in your browser tab: the pattern Feynman called quantum mechanics' "only mystery". EGPT conceptually holds computer science and physics are linked by P=NP and the principle of least action - that is, everything in reality is efficiently computable. The Lean RET, the derivation of EntropyReal from an IIDParticleSource, and the P=NP capstones are modern formalizations of proofs and ideas advanced by Gian-Carlo Rota circa the late 1970s. The EGPT Lean proofs transparently show the most rigorously advanced proofs ever offered for bridging not only quantum and classical mechanics but mathematics and all the other sciences. Watch it run, read its code, and judge for yourself whether this is true P=NP quantum computing.
tile.why: Feynman called it "impossible, absolutely impossible, to explain in any classical way". A ray tracer cannot draw it at all, and solving the light waves directly for a 10 cm tabletop would need about 150,000 times the memory of the Frontier supercomputer and about 400 years of its time.
tile.how: A sphere emitter, walls, two tunnels for the slits and a detector plate. Each particle is an independent cellular automaton following local rules: no wave equation, no amplitudes to add.

still.alt: Three red blocks with blue slit walls between them inside a dark glass box; a cloud of yellow dots hangs above the slits, and below them a flat heat-map plate of blue squares glows yellow-green along a central band.

scenes.prose: The photoelectric effect as absorb/re-emit: an incoming light stream charges an ABSORBING wall — it fills to capacity (watch the stored bar plateau) and radiates lower-dimension quanta out its back, mass exactly conserved. A live chart shows the wall's charge ledger (stored / absorbed / radiated); a second Detector Screen behind the wall counts the radiated photoelectrons as they emerge past it. Incoming light charges the wall, radiated quanta appear beyond it and get counted — the current absorb/radiate drip (the emergent-probability threshold comes later).

scenes.rungTitle: One Emitter at the Canonical Leg
scenes.prose: ONE point source, nothing between it and the plate, and the plate placed at the axial leg D = λ_eff/4 — the leg the published ring formula r_m = (λ/4)·√((2m+1)²+1) was written for, where the "+1" under the root IS the (λ/4)² axial term. At that leg the pattern crosses the wall at TWO points, one above and one below the source, each a quarter-wavelength out: the count-by-y chart standing behind the wall should show a band PAIR at y = 120 and y = 280 on the 600×400 stage, with a sharp minimum just inside each and a flat plateau between them. The plate COUNTS WITHOUT ABSORBING (preset transparent-probe), so the reading is the density at the plate plane rather than a first-arrival caustic, and the quanta fly on to a far-edge sink. λ = 320 px is chosen for resolution: the dip-to-peak structure is 0.025λ wide, so a shorter wavelength would smear it into a hump on this stage. The light is yellow because its fullness is 0.3125 — derived, never forced.

scenes.rungTitle: Two Emitters at the Canonical Leg
scenes.prose: The SAME apparatus with a SECOND point source, separated from the first by exactly d = λ_eff/2 — the strongest-coupling case, since two sources reinforce when their separation is a multiple of λ/2 and the coupling falls as (λ/d)². The plate stays at the same leg D = λ_eff/4 from the emitter plane, with the same chart registered to it. Because each source lays its own band a quarter-wavelength above and below itself, and the two sources sit a half-wavelength apart, source 1's LOWER band and source 2's UPPER band land on the SAME line — the midline y = 200, equidistant from both emitters. So the chart should show a CENTRAL peak where the one-emitter rung has none, flanked by the two outer bands at y = 40 and y = 360. That contrast — no centre with one source, a doubly-reinforced centre with two — is the whole claim, and it is one glance at two graphs.

scenes.rungTitle: Two Slits at the Canonical Leg
scenes.prose: The SAME apparatus as "Two Emitters at the Canonical Leg", but the two point sources are SLIT EXITS in an opaque barrier rather than two free emitters. ONE emitter sits behind the barrier and lights BOTH slits; each slit is a directed Tunnel channel whose exit gate is COLLAPSED and PHASE-RESET, so the mouth stands in for a phase-locked point source at exactly the slit's own y — the same "configured emitter" composition dse-tunnel-rebuild uses. The slit centres sit at the identical y = 120 and y = 280 the two-emitter rung used, separated by the same d = λ_eff/2, and the plate sits at the identical leg D = λ_eff/4 — now measured from the slit exit plane, this apparatus's new source plane. If the slit is a faithful point source, the two rungs must draw the SAME picture: a central peak at y = 200 (source 1's lower band and source 2's upper band coincide there) flanked by outer bands at y = 40 and y = 360.

scenes.rungTitle: One Slit at the Canonical Leg
scenes.prose: The companion arm to "Two Slits at the Canonical Leg": the IDENTICAL apparatus (same emitter, same barrier, same slit-1 aperture at y=120, same leg D, same plate, same chart) with the SECOND slit walled off — one aperture instead of two. A slit exit is a phase-locked point source at its own y, so with only slit 1 open the surviving population is governed by ONE source at y=120: its own ring ladder predicts bands at y=40, y=200, and y=360 (the same three y positions the two-slit rung shows), not a single broad structureless lobe centred on the open slit. This is the actual double-slit claim — presence and position of structure from purely stochastic, non-interacting particles — read as one glance between the two charts.

A cavity of absorbing walls held at a target number of quanta by its own thermostat. Leaves collide and merge into parent frames; a frame's fullness is its frequency, so what leaks out of the slit is a spectrum of frame sizes. The Planck-like curve emerges from collisions — no energy quanta assumed.

tile.title: Blackbody
tile.tile: Particles in a box. The Planck curve appears; no quanta assumed.
tile.what: A hot box of jostling particles glows red, and light spills out through a slit in its side. The Planck curve appears; no energy quanta are assumed.
tile.why: Classical physics, the Rayleigh–Jeans law, predicts infinite energy at high frequencies, the "ultraviolet catastrophe". There is no settled traditional way to compute the plasma physics behind Planck's 1900 law from first principles.
tile.how: A box, a thermostat that keeps it hot, and an absorbing wall that catches whatever escapes. Colliding particles merge into larger frames, and how full a frame is sets its colour. Independent cellular automata, no equations.

still.alt: A grey box packed with glowing red blobs and tiny yellow dots, with dots and a few red blobs streaming out of an opening on its right side.

scenes.prose: Two laser inputs drive rail traces into an XOR gate (SUM) and an AND gate (CARRY). A gate's valve opens only when its two input ammeters read its logic, so the circuit settles onto the half-adder's answer, read as the current on each grounded readout. No search algorithm runs.

tile.title: Circuit SAT
tile.tile: A half-adder settles on its own answer. No search algorithm runs.
tile.what: A half-adder settles on its own answer, you are watching electricity simulated in a circuit component live in your browser tab. Quanta (electrons or photons if you like) flow down the wires into two gates; with input A on, the SUM line fills with flowing quanta and nothing flows along CARRY. No search algorithm runs.
tile.why: Circuit satisfiability, the canonical P vs NP problem of computer science, is also a physical question about real circuits. Every modern circuit is built out of half-adders - put some constant number C of half-adders together and if simulating one is polynomial then C × polynomial is still polynomial. No polynomial-time algorithm is supposed to exist, so the usual way to find an input that satisfies a circuit is to search for one. The EGPT proofs, machine-checked in Lean, show that P=NP.
tile.how: Two logic gates, the wires between them and an emitter on each input - the half-adder electrical circuit simulation settles in your browser in polynomial time, effectively at once. A gate opens only when its inputs carry the pattern it stands for, so the circuit settles into its answer. Independent cellular automata, no equations. EGPT conceptually holds computer science and physics are linked by P=NP and the principle of least action - that is, everything in reality is efficiently computable. The Lean RET, the derivation of EntropyReal from an IIDParticleSource, and the P=NP capstones are modern formalizations of proofs and ideas advanced by Gian-Carlo Rota circa the late 1970s. The EGPT Lean proofs transparently show the most rigorously advanced proofs ever offered for bridging not only quantum and classical mechanics but mathematics and all the other sciences. Watch the answer emerge with no search, read the code, and judge for yourself whether this is true P=NP quantum computing.
tile.controls: It starts with input A on. Click the input A and input B toggles (bottom left) to switch each input on or off. Read the two outputs on the right: the top one is SUM (A xor B), the bottom one is CARRY (A and B). An output with quanta flowing along it reads 1; an empty one reads 0.

still.alt: A circuit of blue bars on black; two lit input lines on the left feed two gates, the top output line carries a long stream of orange beads to the right, and the bottom output holds only a short, stalled cluster.

scenes.prose: One radial burst of leaves with no initial momentum, in a world that generates parent frames top-down. The uniform field clumps into filaments and voids with no gravity law and no cosmological constant.

tile.title: Big Bang
tile.tile: A uniform field. Filaments and voids form. No gravity law, no constant.
tile.what: One burst fills the space, and structure emerges on its own. This is a fractal at its heart - it could be quantum emergence or large cosmic structures ... one set of rules from which attractive forces are a matter of your chosen unit of scale. This simulation is not meant as an assertion of what the correct scales are; it is an exploration of how emergence and scale are related.
tile.why: Large-scale cosmic structure requires gravitational attraction tuned over 13.8 billion years, and a simulation has to compute that gravity across the whole span.
tile.how: One point source, and a world that builds larger frames from the top down. No gravity law, no cosmological constant, no equations.

still.alt: A ragged red cloud of overlapping glowing discs laced with fine gold specks, clumped and broken at its edges, on black.

scenes.prose: Forty-eight quarks in a proton frame, the proton and one electron in a stationary atom frame. Each parent's compress pulls its children one pixel toward its centre each tick, so the structure binds and holds with no force law and no quantum numbers.

tile.title: Atomic model
tile.tile: Particles bind and stay bound. Stable orbits without quantum numbers.
tile.what: Quarks pack into a proton and stay bound, and an electron keeps its place in the atom around it. Stable orbits, without quantum numbers. Like the Big Bang, this simulation is not meant as an assertion of what the correct scales are; it is an exploration of how emergence and scale are related - the engine lets you set stable containment, or experiment with scale so that stability is emergent.
tile.why: Classical physics says an orbiting electron radiates its energy away and spirals into the nucleus in about 16 trillionths of a second. Textbook physics avoids that only by assuming quantised energy levels.
tile.how: Frames nested three layers deep: quarks in a proton, the proton and an electron in an atom. Each parent draws its children one step toward its centre every tick, and binding emerges from that. No force equation.

still.alt: A large dark-red disc with a brighter red core; at the core's left edge a small violet ball sits in a tight cluster of pale beads, and one lone pale bead lies further out at lower right.

scenes.prose: The omni source released into all three dimensions — a true 3D ball of quanta rendered with three.js, orbit-able with the mouse or the on-screen camera joysticks.

The finale — the 3D omni point source dressed as a star: a dense (mass-16, fullness-1) warm-cool glowing core with volumetric god-rays and a shimmer of heat. The same walk that drew the pool, now the sun.

tile.title: A sun
tile.tile: Put light in the scene and let light do what light does. No Standard Model; god-rays from particle density.
tile.what: Put light in the scene and let light do what light does: a blazing sun, its glow and god rays spreading in every direction through the space around it.
tile.why: Games paint glow and god rays onto the finished picture as a separate screen effect, aimed from where the sun is on the screen rather than from any light in the scene.
tile.how: One sphere emitter, shining in every direction. The god rays are rendered from the density of the particles themselves. No Standard Model, no equations, and the engine does not know whether you are looking at a star, a candle flame or an atom.

still.alt: A white-hot sun with a golden halo and fine rays fanning out in every direction across a dim, grainy space.

scenes.prose: The mirror in a 3D scene, FACE-ON: a directional +x beam hits a mirror SLAB (a box you can orbit around) square on its drawn face and bounces STRAIGHT BACK — beam in, recolored beam out along the same line, nothing continuing past the plate, from every camera angle (an actual mirror). Orbit (LOOK/drag) to see the retro-reflection in three dimensions; ROTATE the mirror (the orientation slider) to steer the exit by the same 2θ law as the 2D mirror — identical physics, now a box in space (2D≡3D).

The absorbing wall as a 3D slab: a volumetric (spherical) source sprays quanta in three dimensions into a wall SLAB that absorbs them into its own real mass, fills to capacity, and radiates lower-dimension leaves back out — mass exactly conserved. Orbit the camera to watch the spray soak into the box from every angle (2D≡3D).

The detector screen as a 3D slab with a live in-scene chart: a volumetric source sprays into a Detector Screen SLAB (destroy + count); a first-class LiveChart panel — placed in the scene beside the detector — plots the running arrivals as the sim runs, textured into the 3D view. Orbit to see the detector box and its chart in space (the basis for a 3D fringe readout).

Seven head-on lanes of equal-mass voxel pairs at seven depths, from feather-light to rigid. Density sets how hard the bodies are; contact is identical on every axis. The same engine that makes light makes mechanics.

tile.title: 3D Collisions Lab
tile.tile: Balls in a box. Contact, momentum, settling. The same engine that makes light makes mechanics; no second physics.
tile.what: Balls in a box, in seven lanes coloured red to violet by density. Each pair flies together and collides: the hard ones bounce cleanly, the soft ones press into each other before parting. Contact, momentum, settling. This is a "Collisions Lab" because it is up to you to find the capacity-and-fill relationships that produce the desired elastic vs inelastic collisions at your desired scale.
tile.why: In a game engine, collisions come from a separate physics engine, such as NVIDIA PhysX, solving rigid-body equations beside the renderer that draws the light. Two systems, two sets of rules.
tile.how: The same engine that makes the light in the other scenes makes these collisions: pairs of the same frames at seven densities. No second physics, no equations.

still.alt: Pairs of shiny balls, red, orange, yellow, green and violet, meeting in mid-air against black.

scenes.prose: A gun fires and the smoke emerges. Your challenge: make the bullet self-propelled.
